title: Ezekiel Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 18.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 18, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD came unto me again
What mean ye, that ye use this proverb
As I live, saith the Lord GOD
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the LORD came unto me again
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned in the chapter is the statement, 'The word of the LORD came unto me again', found in Ezekiel 18:1.

questions.question: What proverb concerning the land of Israel is mentioned in Ezekiel 18?
options: The fathers have eaten sour grapes
The children have set their teeth on edge
He that hath not given forth upon usury
questions.correctAnswer: The fathers have eaten sour grapes
questions.explanation: The proverb mentioned is 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes', as stated in Ezekiel 18:2.

questions.question: What does the Lord GOD say about the use of the proverb in Israel?
options: It shall not be used anymore
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be used anymore
questions.explanation: The Lord GOD declares that they shall not have occasion to use the proverb any more, as stated in Ezekiel 18:3.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 18, whose souls are said to belong to the Lord?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Behold, all souls are mine', indicating that all souls belong to the Lord, as found in Ezekiel 18:4.

questions.question: What must a man do to be considered just in Ezekiel 18?
options: He must eat upon the mountains
He must do that which is lawful and right
questions.correctAnswer: He must do that which is lawful and right
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:5 states that a man is considered just if he does that which is lawful and right.

questions.question: What actions are NOT associated with a just man in Ezekiel 18?
questions.explanation: A just man does not defile his neighbour's wife, as stated in Ezekiel 18:6.

questions.question: What does a just man do for the hungry according to Ezekiel 18?
questions.explanation: The verse states that a just man gives his bread to the hungry, as stated in Ezekiel 18:7.

questions.question: What is said about usury in relation to a just man in Ezekiel 18?
options: He does not give forth upon usury
questions.correctAnswer: He does not give forth upon usury
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:8 states that a just man does not give forth upon usury.

questions.question: What will happen to a just man according to Ezekiel 18?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:9 states that the just man shall surely live.

questions.question: What kind of son can a just man beget according to Ezekiel 18?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:10 refers to a son that is a robber and a shedder of blood.

questions.question: What duties does the son mentioned in Ezekiel 18:11 NOT perform?
options: He has not eaten upon the mountains
He has defiled his neighbour's wife
He has restored his neighbour's pledge
questions.correctAnswer: He has defiled his neighbour's wife
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:11 states that the son does not perform the duties of a just man and has defiled his neighbour's wife.

questions.question: A just man will not defile his neighbour's wife.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Ezekiel 18:6 clearly states that a just man does not defile his neighbour's wife.

questions.question: All souls belong to the Lord according to Ezekiel 18.
questions.explanation: This statement is true as Ezekiel 18:4 states, 'Behold, all souls are mine'.

questions.question: A just man can take increase according to Ezekiel 18.
questions.explanation: This statement is false because Ezekiel 18:8 states that a just man does not take increase.

questions.question: The proverb about the fathers and sour grapes is found in Ezekiel 18:5.
questions.explanation: This statement is false as the proverb is mentioned in Ezekiel 18:2, not 18:5.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What actions are described in Ezekiel 18:12 that lead to condemnation?
options: Hath oppressed the poor and needy
Hath given bread to the hungry
questions.correctAnswer: Hath oppressed the poor and needy
questions.explanation: This is correct as Ezekiel 18:12 lists the actions leading to condemnation, highlighting oppression and moral failings.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 18:13 promise will happen if someone engages in all these abominations?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:13 states that engaging in abominations results in death, emphasizing the seriousness of sin.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 18:14, what is the condition of a son who sees his father's sins but does not commit them?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:14 indicates that a son who does not follow in his father's sinful ways will live.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 18:15 say about a person who has not lifted up his eyes to idols?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:15 describes a person who avoids idolatry as being righteous, which is key to living.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 18:16, what actions demonstrate a righteous person?
options: Hath lifted up his eyes to the idols
Hath covered the naked with a garment
questions.correctAnswer: Hath covered the naked with a garment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:16 lists acts of kindness and justice as characteristics of a righteous person.

questions.question: What is the consequence for the son of a wicked father, according to Ezekiel 18:17?
options: He shall die for his father's sins
He shall not die for his father's iniquity
He shall be judged with his father
He shall inherit his father's sins
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not die for his father's iniquity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:17 clarifies that the son will not be punished for his father's sins if he lives righteously.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 18:19 ask about the relationship between father and son regarding iniquity?
options: Does the son bear the iniquity of the father?
Is the father judged by the son's actions?
Do both share in the same fate?
Does righteousness pass from father to son?
questions.correctAnswer: Does the son bear the iniquity of the father?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:19 poses this question to challenge the idea of inherited guilt, emphasizing personal responsibility.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 18:20 say about the soul that sins?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20 clearly states that the soul that sins will face death, reinforcing the seriousness of sin.

questions.question: What is promised in Ezekiel 18:21 if the wicked turn from their sins?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:21 assures that turning from wickedness leads to life, emphasizing the possibility of redemption.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 18:22, what happens to a person's transgressions if they live righteously?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:22 states that a person's past sins will not be held against them if they live righteously.

questions.question: If a person engages in righteous behavior, what does Ezekiel 18:9 state about their fate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:9 promises life for those who walk in righteousness and keep God's judgments.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 18:4, whose souls are ultimately under God's authority?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:4 establishes that all souls belong to God, emphasizing His sovereignty over life and death.

questions.question: Is it true that a son bears the iniquity of his father according to Ezekiel 18:20?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20 states clearly that the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, emphasizing individual accountability.

questions.question: Is it true that the soul that sins shall live according to Ezekiel 18:20?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20 asserts that the soul that sins shall die, making this statement false.

questions.question: Is it true that a righteous person will suffer for the sins of their father according to Ezekiel 18:17?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:17 clarifies that the righteous shall not die for their father's iniquity, making this statement false.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 18.

questions.question: What is the Lord's desire regarding the wicked, according to Ezekiel 18:23?
options: He takes pleasure in their death.
He wants them to remain wicked.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:23 states that the Lord does not take pleasure in the death of the wicked but desires that they return from their ways and live.

questions.question: What happens to the righteousness of a righteous man who turns away from it, according to Ezekiel 18:24?
options: His righteousness will not be mentioned.
questions.correctAnswer: His righteousness will not be mentioned.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:24 indicates that if a righteous man turns away and commits iniquity, all his previous righteousness will not be mentioned.

questions.question: According to Ezekiel 18:25, how do the people of Israel view the Lord's ways?
options: They believe His ways are just.
They think His ways are unequal.
questions.correctAnswer: They think His ways are unequal.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:25 records the house of Israel claiming that the way of the Lord is not equal, prompting the Lord to challenge this view.

questions.question: What must a wicked man do to save his soul alive, according to Ezekiel 18:27?
options: Repent and do what is lawful and right.
Follow the example of the righteous.
questions.correctAnswer: Repent and do what is lawful and right.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:27 states that when the wicked man turns from his wickedness and does what is lawful and right, he shall save his soul alive.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 18:30 urge the house of Israel to do?
options: Repent and turn from their transgressions.
questions.correctAnswer: Repent and turn from their transgressions.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:30 commands the house of Israel to repent and turn from all their transgressions to avoid ruin.

questions.question: What does the Lord have no pleasure in, according to Ezekiel 18:32?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:32 explicitly states that the Lord has no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, emphasizing His desire for repentance.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shuv' in Ezekiel 18:23 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Shuv' (שׁוּב) means 'to return' or 'to turn back,' as seen in Ezekiel 18:23 where the Lord desires the wicked to return from their ways.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ezekiel 18:30 when the Lord calls for repentance?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 18:30, the Lord directly addresses the house of Israel, which is an example of apostrophe, as He speaks to them as a distinct audience.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of individual accountability found in Ezekiel 18:20?
questions.explanation: Romans 14:12 states that each of us will give an account of ourselves to God, echoing the theme of individual accountability in Ezekiel 18:20.

questions.question: Which verse in the New Testament connects to the repentance theme in Ezekiel 18:30?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:38 calls for repentance and baptism in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, paralleling the call to repentance in Ezekiel 18:30.

questions.question: What verse directly precedes Ezekiel 18:32?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:31 directly precedes 18:32, where the Lord urges Israel to cast away their transgressions and make a new heart and spirit.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 18:28 emphasize about the wicked who repent?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:28 emphasizes that the wicked man who considers and turns away from his transgressions shall surely live and not die.

questions.question: The statement 'The soul that sinneth, it shall die' is found in which verse?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:4 states, 'The soul that sinneth, it shall die,' establishing the principle of individual accountability for sin.

questions.question: True or False: The Lord has no pleasure in the death of the wicked according to Ezekiel 18:32.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:32 clearly states that the Lord has no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, revealing His desire for repentance.

questions.question: True or False: The righteous are punished for the iniquities of their fathers according to Ezekiel 18:20.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20 states that the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, emphasizing individual accountability for sin.

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 18:4 teach about individual responsibility for sin?
options: The soul that sinneth, it shall die
The iniquity of the father shall be upon the son
God excuses sin committed by descendants
questions.correctAnswer: The soul that sinneth, it shall die
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:4 teaches clearly that each soul is responsible for its own sin and will die for that sin, emphasizing individual accountability before God.

questions.question: What doctrine about repentance and divine mercy is presented in Ezekiel 18:21?
options: If the wicked turn from all his sins, he shall surely live
The wicked are condemned without hope of repentance
Only the righteous will be saved regardless of repentance
Repentance cannot change one’s eternal destiny
questions.correctAnswer: If the wicked turn from all his sins, he shall surely live
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:21 affirms that a wicked person who repents and obeys God's statutes will live, highlighting God's mercy and the possibility of salvation through repentance.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the transfer of guilt between generations is taught in Ezekiel 18:20?
options: The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father
Guilt is automatically inherited from ancestors
Collective punishment is just for familial sins
God holds entire families accountable for one sinner
questions.correctAnswer: The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20 explicitly rejects the notion of inherited guilt, teaching that each person bears responsibility for their own sin only.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 18:23 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:23 shows God’s longsuffering because He expresses no pleasure in the death of the wicked but desires their repentance and life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in Ezekiel 18:25 regarding God's justice?
questions.explanation: In Ezekiel 18:25, God challenges the accusation that His way is unequal and affirms that His way is just and equal, highlighting His attribute of justice.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 18 prepare the theological ground for New Testament teachings on personal repentance and judgment?
options: By emphasizing individual responsibility and the possibility of turning to life
By teaching collective punishment for corporate sin
By denying any need for repentance
By asserting predestination without human response
questions.correctAnswer: By emphasizing individual responsibility and the possibility of turning to life
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18 sets the stage for the New Testament by focusing on personal repentance and judgment, aligning with teachings like those in Acts 17:30 and 2 Corinthians 5:10.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Ezekiel 18:31 make with the concept of spiritual renewal found elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It calls for a new heart and a new spirit, echoing Jeremiah 31:33
It mandates ritual sacrifices for atonement
It denies the need for internal transformation
It emphasizes national rather than personal repentance
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for a new heart and a new spirit, echoing Jeremiah 31:33
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:31’s call for a new heart and spirit connects to the promise of the new covenant in Jeremiah 31:33, emphasizing inward transformation as key to repentance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 18:4 and 18:20 teach about the nature of sin and judgment?
options: Individual responsibility for sin without inherited guilt
Universal imputation of sin to all family members
questions.correctAnswer: Individual responsibility for sin without inherited guilt
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that each soul is responsible for its own sin and will die for it, denying the transfer of guilt between father and son.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine mercy and human repentance is taught by combining Ezekiel 18:21 and 18:22?
options: Repentance results in forgiveness and the forgetting of past transgressions
Repentance is insufficient to alter divine judgment
God remembers all sins despite repentance
Forgiveness is only partial and conditional
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance results in forgiveness and the forgetting of past transgressions
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:21-22 teaches that when the wicked repent and do right, their past sins will not be remembered and they will live, highlighting full forgiveness by God.

questions.question: What do Ezekiel 18:24 and 18:26 together teach about the consequences of turning away from righteousness or wickedness?
options: Abandoning righteousness results in death; abandoning wickedness results in life
Turning from wickedness has no effect on one’s destiny
Righteousness guarantees eternal life regardless of later actions
God’s judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to behavior
questions.correctAnswer: Abandoning righteousness results in death; abandoning wickedness results in life
questions.explanation: These verses teach that forsaking righteousness leads to death, while forsaking wickedness leads to life, emphasizing the dynamic nature of repentance and judgment.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Ezekiel 18:20-22 teaches that God is unfair because children are punished for their fathers’ sins. What does Ezekiel 18:20-22 actually teach?
options: Each person is judged for their own sin, and repentance leads to forgiveness
Children always bear the punishment for their fathers’ sins
God arbitrarily punishes families for one member’s wickedness
Righteousness is inherited without regard to personal actions
questions.correctAnswer: Each person is judged for their own sin, and repentance leads to forgiveness
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:20-22 clearly states that the soul who sins dies, not the son for the father, and that repentance results in life, underscoring individual judgment and mercy.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of righteousness and justice is taught in Ezekiel 18:5-9?
options: Righteousness involves obeying God’s statutes and practicing justice toward others
Righteousness is merely ritual observance without ethical implications
Justice is secondary to ceremonial purity
Human actions cannot affect divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness involves obeying God’s statutes and practicing justice toward others
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:5-9 outlines righteousness as both lawful conduct and just treatment of neighbors, showing ethical obedience as key to life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially highlighted in Ezekiel 18:32 regarding God's attitude toward death and repentance?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18:32 emphasizes God’s mercy, stating He takes no pleasure in the death of the sinner but desires repentance and life.

questions.question: How does the narrative arc of Ezekiel 18 connect with the broader biblical theme of covenantal accountability?
options: It insists on personal responsibility within the covenant community
It denies the covenantal obligations of Israel
It teaches that covenant blessings are automatic for descendants
It promotes ignoring the covenant statutes
questions.correctAnswer: It insists on personal responsibility within the covenant community
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 18 stresses individual accountability before God, a key theme in covenant theology where each member is responsible to uphold God’s laws.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 18:10-13 and 18:14-17 teach about generational sin and righteousness?
options: A son is not condemned for the sins of a wicked father if he chooses righteousness
Children are condemned regardless of their own choices
Righteousness is inherited regardless of personal conduct
One’s fate is sealed by parental sin
questions.correctAnswer: A son is not condemned for the sins of a wicked father if he chooses righteousness
questions.explanation: These verses contrast a wicked father and a righteous son, showing that the son will live if he does right, emphasizing personal responsibility over inherited guilt.
